facts.fact: TechCabal reports that NINAuth, NIMC's digital identity authentication service, launched in 2025 and is still being refined, with full integration dependent on the NIMS 2.0 rollout.

The World Bank's August 2026 report, as reported by TechCabal, puts NINs issued at 117.5 million people at 30 June 2026, about 49% of the 237.5 million population (computed here), against a 180 million December 2026 target.

NGA.note: Children under 16 hold 26.3 million NINs, but no number at birth is stated.

facts.fact: TechCabal reports that NIMC implements the ID4D project and is enrolling 1.5 to 1.8 million people a month and issuing NINs.

NGA.note: NIN-linked services are named but no public register keyed on the NIN is stated.

facts.fact: The World Bank report, as reported by TechCabal, says NIMC had issued NINs to 117.5 million people out of 134.6 million enrolments at 30 June 2026.

TechCabal reports that enrolment captures demographic and biometric data and that issuance follows processing, validation and deduplication against the national database, as explained by two commentators.
The World Bank's August 2026 assessment says the NIMS 2.0 system integrator contract, built around MOSIP, was being finalised, with implementation expected to take about 18 months.
